children: U.S. lawmakers unveiled a bipartisan tax credit for film and television production on Thursday, starting what they hope will be a sprint to turn it into law in Congress's post-election session.

The bill would create a base tax credit worth 20% of the labor costs associated with a production, and it aims to counter other countries' incentives. The credit could climb as high as 30% for productions that qualify for bonus incentives. Those bonuses include benefits for independent productions and projects in certain rural areas or disaster zones.

"We have never been closer to getting this done than today," said Sen. Adam Schiff (D., Calif.), a frequent critic of President Trump who is working with the administration on this issue. "We have this rare confluence of events that makes this really possible."

Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina is the lead Senate Republican sponsor. Key House backers include Reps. Brian Jack (R., Ga.), Laura Friedman (D., Calif.), Linda Sanchez (D., Calif), Judy Chu (D., Calif.) and Nathaniel Moran (R., Texas).
